judge_reasoning: The Knight reaches only 6 power, not 7: base 2, +2 from the two Gideon emblems, +1 from Temmet, and +1 from Behind the Scenes. Although Temmet makes it unblockable, it deals only 6 damage, leaving the opponent at 1 life.
model_solution:
1. Main phase 1: Tap two Irrigated Farmlands for {W}{U} and cast **Temmet, Vizier of Naktamun**. (It can't attack this turn, but its combat trigger is what matters.)
2. Still in main phase 1: activate **Gideon, Ally of Zendikar's −4** (loyalty 4 → 0, he goes to the graveyard). You now have a **second** Gideon emblem — emblems ignore the legend rule, so both "Creatures you control get +1/+1" effects apply. The Knight Ally token is now 4/4.
3. Move to combat. At the beginning of combat, **Temmet's triggered ability** targets the Knight Ally token: it gets +1/+1 until end of turn and **can't be blocked this turn** (now 5/5, unblockable).
4. Tap the remaining two Irrigated Farmlands (one for {W}) and all three Swamps to activate **Behind the Scenes' {4}{W}** ability: creatures you control get the pump until end of turn, putting the Knight token at 7 power (2/2 base, +1/+1 from each of the two emblems, +1/+1 from Temmet, plus the Behind the Scenes pump).
5. Declare the Knight Ally token as the lone attacker. Because of Temmet it can't be blocked (and the Seraph couldn't block it anyway thanks to skulk), so no blocking decision by the opponent matters.
6. Combat damage: the unblockable Knight token deals 7 damage to the opponent, taking them from 7 to 0. You win.

Puzzle conventions:
Winning
Unless otherwise stated, you must win the puzzle by inflicting lethal damage to your opponent before the turn ends. This can be as late as during the cleanup step if necessary. Your solution must work for all possible outcomes, such as your opponent’s actions and blocking decisions (see below.)
Phase
Unless otherwise stated, you begin each puzzle at the beginning of your first main phase. You have already drawn a card and gone past upkeep triggers. You have not yet played a land, cast any spells, activated any abilities of permanents on the battlefield, or attacked.
Your Opponent’s Resources / Actions
Unless otherwise stated, your opponent has no cards in hand and no other permanents in play (including no lands – despite the lack of realism there.) This means the only actions you need to consider are activated abilities with no mana cost. Most puzzles with opponent actions will offer more information on this.
Blocking
You cannot assume that your opponent will block a certain way, unless they are somehow forced to. Your solution must satisfy all possible blocking scenarios, even ones that would seem strange in a regular game, and always deal lethal in order to be correct.
Dice
Sometimes you will see six-sided dice placed on cards. These are meant to indicate counters, of whatever type is most reasonable to be there. On most creatures they will be +1/+1 counters, on most artifacts and lands they will be charge counters, and on most Planeswalkers they will be loyalty counters.
If the card specifies a type of counter itself, however (like Icatian Javelineers or Raging Ravine), that will dictate which type it is. 
For -1/-1 counters, we will use a separate graphic to avoid confusion.
Zones
Unless otherwise stated, all zones not displayed are empty. Neither you nor your opponent have cards in graveyards or in exile.
Cards Drawn from Libraries
In any puzzle in which either player might draw cards or otherwise access their library, the puzzle will stipulate some known or assumed information about the library.
Most commonly, this will be a statement that you should assume that the cards remaining in libraries are to be assumed to be irrelevant to the puzzle.
Your Life
Occasionally, your own life total might appear to matter – for cards like Anguished Unmaking, for example. If we require you to consider your own life total in a puzzle, it will be displayed.
If your life total is not shown, you may assume it is irrelevant and effectively infinite.

When you are ready to answer, put your final winning line inside <solution> tags:

<solution>
1. First step...
2. Second step...
</solution>

Your line must be legal under the rules and must win against all possible opponent responses and blocking decisions.

4862:702.118. Skulk
4864:702.118a Skulk is an evasion ability.
4866:702.118b A creature with skulk can’t be blocked by creatures with greater power. (See rule 509, “Declare Blockers Step.”)
4868:702.118c Multiple instances of skulk on the same creature are redundant.
8892:Skulk
8893:A keyword ability that restricts how a creature may be blocked. See rule 702.118, “Skulk.”

28:114. Emblems
580:109.1. An object is an ability on the stack, a card, a copy of a card, a token, a spell, a permanent, or an emblem.
600:109.4c An emblem is controlled by the player who puts it into the command zone. See rule 114, “Emblems.”
801:113.6p Abilities of emblems, plane cards, vanguard cards, scheme cards, and conspiracy cards function in the command zone. See rule 114, “Emblems”; rule 901, “Planechase”; rule 902, “Vanguard”; rule 904, “Archenemy”; and rule 905, “Conspiracy Draft.”
824:114. Emblems
826:114.1. Some effects put emblems into the command zone. An emblem is a marker used to represent an object that has one or more abilities, but usually no other characteristics.
828:114.2. An effect that creates an emblem is written “[Player] gets an emblem with [ability].” This means that [player] puts an emblem with [ability] into the command zone. The emblem is both owned and controlled by that player.
830:114.3. An emblem has no characteristics other than the abilities defined by the effect that created it. In particular, an emblem has no types, no mana cost, and no color. Most emblems also have no name.
832:114.4. Abilities of emblems function in the command zone.
834:114.5. An emblem is neither a card nor a permanent. Emblem isn’t a card type.
2106:408.2. Emblems may be created in the command zone. See rule 114, “Emblems.”
2738:607.1d Abilities printed on two objects can be linked if one object is a token, emblem, or nontoken permanent and the second object was the source of the ability that either created the token or emblem or put that nontoken permanent onto the battlefield. In these cases, the abilities fit the criteria listed for one of the different kinds of linked abilities in rule 607.2 except they are printed on two objects rather than one.
3755:701.54c If a player doesn’t have an emblem named The Ring at the time the Ring tempts them, they get an emblem named The Ring before choosing a creature to be their Ring-bearer. The Ring has “Your Ring-bearer is legendary and can’t be blocked by creatures with greater power.” As long as the Ring has tempted that player two or more times, it has “Whenever your Ring-bearer attacks, draw a card, then discard a card.” As long as the Ring has tempted that player three or more times, it has “Whenever your Ring-bearer becomes blocked by a creature, the blocking creature’s controller sacrifices it at end of combat.” As long as the Ring has tempted that player four or more times, it has “Whenever your Ring-bearer deals combat damage to a player, each opponent loses 3 life.”
7730:Emblem
7731:An emblem is a marker used to represent an object that has one or more abilities, but no other characteristics. See rule 114, “Emblems.”
8466:An ability on the stack, a card, a copy of a card, an emblem, a token, a spell, or a permanent. See rule 109, “Objects.”
8790:An emblem that may be created at the time the Ring tempts you. See rule 701.54, “The Ring Tempts You.”
8793:A keyword action that causes a player to choose a creature they control to be their legendary Ring-bearer and may cause them to create an emblem called The Ring. See rule 701.54, “The Ring Tempts You.”

The opponent has 7 life and three blockers (Seraph 4/4 indestructible, Sparring Mummy 3/3, Labyrinth Guardian 2/3).

Key facts I checked:

- **Gideon can't get through.** If I use his +1 he's a 6/6 (5/5 + emblem), and skulk (702.118b — "can't be blocked by creatures with greater power") does nothing at that power, so one of the three blockers just eats him. My removal (Dead Weight, Anguished Unmaking, Illusory Wrappings) can only account for **two** blockers with 7 mana, never all three, and shrinking Gideon so skulk works (Illusory Wrappings → 1/3) reduces him to 1 damage. Every "attack with Gideon" line caps out at 4–5 damage.
- **So the whole attack must be the one creature that can be made truly unblockable: the Knight token**, via Temmet's beginning-of-combat trigger ("can't be blocked this turn").
- Then it's just a matter of stacking every available +X/+X on it with exactly 7 mana: the emblem already on the battlefield, a **second** emblem from Gideon's −4 (emblems aren't permanents and aren't subject to the legend rule — rule 114.4/114.5, so both "creatures you control get +1/+1" emblems apply), Temmet's trigger, and Behind the Scenes' pump.

Mana: Temmet = {W}{U} (two Irrigated Farmlands), Behind the Scenes = {4}{W} (third Farmland for {W}, fourth Farmland + 3 Swamps for the {4}). Exactly 7 lands, exactly 7 mana. The removal spells in hand are red herrings — they can't clear a path for Gideon and they compete with the mana needed for the pump.

## Solution

<solution>
1. Main phase 1: Tap two Irrigated Farmlands for {W}{U} and cast **Temmet, Vizier of Naktamun**. (It can't attack this turn, but its combat trigger is what matters.)
2. Still in main phase 1: activate **Gideon, Ally of Zendikar's −4** (loyalty 4 → 0, he goes to the graveyard). You now have a **second** Gideon emblem — emblems ignore the legend rule, so both "Creatures you control get +1/+1" effects apply. The Knight Ally token is now 4/4.
3. Move to combat. At the beginning of combat, **Temmet's triggered ability** targets the Knight Ally token: it gets +1/+1 until end of turn and **can't be blocked this turn** (now 5/5, unblockable).
4. Tap the remaining two Irrigated Farmlands (one for {W}) and all three Swamps to activate **Behind the Scenes' {4}{W}** ability: creatures you control get the pump until end of turn, putting the Knight token at 7 power (2/2 base, +1/+1 from each of the two emblems, +1/+1 from Temmet, plus the Behind the Scenes pump).
5. Declare the Knight Ally token as the lone attacker. Because of Temmet it can't be blocked (and the Seraph couldn't block it anyway thanks to skulk), so no blocking decision by the opponent matters.
6. Combat damage: the unblockable Knight token deals 7 damage to the opponent, taking them from 7 to 0. You win.
</solution>
